revision_history.description: Automated review pass authored in the same session as the records it covers. It is NOT an independent review: the reviewing role is the authoring role and the runtime is the same one that wrote the artifacts. Per master-prompt clause 2.9 that makes it an automated review and nothing more.

revision_history.author: quality_engineer
revision_history.description: Provenance repair by a separate session (opencode-2026-10-01-provenance-repair), not a re-review. All 2 reviewed_ids digests in this record were re-derived from the artefact files as they stand on disk in the correct profile (synthetic_reference).  None of the named artefacts has been revised since this review was issued; every digest here is digest-only drift, so the technical review still covers the content these digests now name.  2 entry(ies) carried the literal string 'placeholder' with no note; a measured digest is now recorded because the artefact file exists.  The findings, dispositions, scope, checklist and reviewer_identity of the original pass are untouched by this repair. The digest refresh does not carry the weight of a re-review: the original reviewer session did not examine the current revision of the revised artefacts, and no substantive re-examination was performed here.

reviewer_identity.note: Automated review performed in a single AI coding-agent session. The model identifier is the identifier exposed to this session's runtime; no platform-issued session id was available, so session_id is a locally chosen label for this run and is not a platform-issued identifier. The reviewing role is the same role that authored the records, so this pass has NO independence from the work it reviews and must not be read as confirmation. It is recorded as coverage of the review obligation, not as discharge of it.

scope: Every record in ids_b at revision 1. Findings were raised against records this pass authored, so no pre-existing canonical record was edited and no pre-existing record is the subject of a finding here.

findings.description: The measurement plan publishes two different denominators for the same coverage metric, because two are in use in the corpus. A reader comparing them would conclude one is wrong.
findings.evidence: MET-02's formula divides by the requirement-artifact count, while the generated coverage output divides by the FSR count. OBS-03 records both figures and states that the choice to publish two is the metric's weakness rather than the data's.

findings.description: The quality-assurance process record states independence that the corpus does not achieve. Every review in the corpus is an automated review produced by the same runtime that wrote the artifacts, and master-prompt clause 2.9 says that is not organisational independence.
findings.evidence: Read from FB2-SUP-QAP-000001's accountable_role.independence field, which states the gap in its own text, and confirmed by reading the reviewer_identity of all twelve pre-existing review records and the three this pass authored.

findings.description: One of the three improvement records has a negative result: its metric moved by zero and its verdict is insufficient_evidence. It is recorded deliberately so the improvement set is not a set of successes.
findings.evidence: OBS-06 records 6 instances and 0 acknowledgement records; the arithmetic in the record states 0 - 0 = 0.

findings.description: The service instruction's post-service check exercises only the main reaction path, so an item whose main path is defective would pass it.
findings.evidence: Read of SVC-05's steps against the requirement in FB2-PRD-EOL-000001's station ST-05, which separately requires the independent hardware path to be exercised. The two records disagree in coverage and the disagreement is recorded on both sides rather than resolved by copying the coverage across.

dispositions.action: Not resolved. Both denominators are published and OBS-03 names the difference. Picking one would hide a real inconsistency in the corpus's own outputs.

Not resolved and not resolvable by this pass. The independence gap is stated in the process record itself and registered as risk RSK-003 with residual exposure equal to inherent. The only fix is to engage a human reviewer, which is outside what this corpus can do.
Accepted as the honest outcome. The record exists partly so that the improvement set contains a non-success and a reader cannot infer that every change works.
Not resolved. Both records state their coverage and the gap between them is visible. Neither was edited to match the other.

limitations: Automated review only, and not independent: the reviewing role authored several of the records it reviews and no human has seen any of them.

These records are fictional and describe a project that does not exist. The review checked their internal consistency and their conformance to the schemas that state what each must contain; it cannot check their realism, because there is nothing to check them against.

Every supporting-process instance carries a non-conformance, and the review confirmed that each non-conformance is a real shortfall in the record rather than a token gesture. Two of the process records therefore fail their own acceptance criteria and say so.

Every post-development record states that no step has been executed and that it authorises nothing on real equipment. The review confirmed the statements are present and mutually consistent, and that no record implies an execution.

The service and decommissioning records were reviewed against each other for contradictions about who owns end-of-life risk. They agree: the service record delivers the assumptions and the decommissioning record states them. The agreement was checked; neither agreement nor disagreement could be checked against a real organisation.
